activities.caption: true or false — is a virus alive?
activities.name: clVirusJudge

statements.s: The flu virus does not respire, excrete or grow.
statements.why: It fails most of the MRS GREN checklist — that is why biologists class viruses as non-living.

statements.s: A virus is a packaged set of instructions that hijacks another cell's machinery.
statements.why: The hijacking is its only claim to activity — the machinery it uses belongs to the host.

statements.s: Viruses count as living because they reproduce inside cells.
statements.why: Reproduction alone is one job of seven — the checklist demands all of them, done by the organism itself.

statements.s: MRS GREN asks whether a thing does all seven jobs, not just some of them.
statements.why: A candle moves and a crystal grows — but only an organism does all seven.

activities.caption: pair each use of classification with its work
activities.name: clUsesMatch

config.prompt: Classification earns its keep four ways — pair each use with its job:

pairs.right: name an unknown organism with the right tool
a new fungus filed with penicillin's relatives may make antibiotics too
farming, medicine and conservation all say exactly which organism they mean
a classification built on ancestry is a map of history

config.why: The system cannot shelve by colour — its collection evolves, so it files by actual ancestry instead.

activities.anchor: The filing has levels, one inside the other
activities.caption: stack the eight levels, narrowest to widest
activities.name: clLevelsOrder

config.prompt: Folders within folders — put the eight levels in order, narrowest first:
items: species — breeds together to fertile offspring
domain — the widest level of all
config.why: Each level up widens the circle of cousins — at family level the cat joins lions and leopards, at order level dogs and seals, at class level whales and bats.

activities.anchor: Watch the levels do quiet work on a familiar animal
activities.caption: fill the blanks — the cat's address
activities.name: clCatCloze

config.text: The domestic cat's address: Kingdom %%0%% (eats food, no cell walls), Phylum %%1%% (has a backbone), Class %%2%% (fur, milk), Order %%3%% (shearing teeth), Family Felidae (retractile claws), Genus Felis, Species catus.
config.hint: Eight words that sketch the cat's place in the tree of life — an address is a compressed family history.

activities.anchor: an unknown animal lands on a name
activities.caption: run the key yourself — four animals, three forks
activities.name: clKeyBranch

config.root: A dichotomous key is a forked questionnaire of visible features: answer one either/or question at a time and follow where it sends you.

start.text: Fork 1 — does it have feathers or fur?

q2.text: Fork 2 — webbed feet or grasping feet?

q3.text: Fork 3 — tail flattened and scaly, or bushy?

duck.text: It is a duck. Two questions, one name — no expert needed.

owl.text: It is an owl. Note the key routed on visible characters only.

beaver.text: It is a beaver. The key's job is routing, not history.

squirrel.text: It is a squirrel. A key does not have to reflect ancestry.

config.why: Each fork tests one visible character, and after a couple of questions an unknown animal lands on a name — the everyday, hands-on half of classification.

activities.caption: file the organisms by their dividing features
activities.name: clGroupsBuckets

config.prompt: Three of the five big groups — file each organism:

items.label: bacteria — DNA in a loop in the jelly
yeast — absorbing through hyphae, chitin walls
a mushroom — the group's fruiting body
a fern — starch as its store

config.why: Prokaryotes lack the nucleus; fungi have one but absorb dead material; plants make their own sugar. The protoctists are the odds-and-ends drawer — Amoeba, Chlorella, Plasmodium.

activities.caption: find the faulty line — reading the cladogram
activities.name: clCladeSpot

config.prompt: This cladogram answer contains one faulty line — click it:
lines: Every fork on the cladogram is an inferred common ancestor.
A closer fork means closer relatives.
A clade must contain an ancestor and all of its descendants.
'Reptiles' excluding birds is fine, because crocodiles are closer kin to lizards.
Every living species is equally 'evolved' — a bacterium is a cousin with 4 billion years of refinement.
config.correction: Crocodiles are closer kin to BIRDS than to lizards — 'reptiles' excluding birds is a leftover of the old ladder, not a clade.
config.why: The clade rule is what kills the old ladder: a genuine evolutionary group takes an ancestor and all of its descendants, feathers included.

activities.caption: call the magnitude — kinship in one molecule
activities.name: clCytoEstimate

config.prompt: Cytochrome c is a small respiratory protein readable as a molecular clock. Human and chimpanzee differ in zero amino acids. Roughly how many amino acids differ between human and horse?
config.why: About 12 (and about 45 with yeast) — a ladder of kinship measured in a single molecule before genome sequencing existed.
config.context: Calibrated against fossils, the molecular clock dates branch points where no fossils exist.
